newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India comes off lows, business seen.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India comes off lows, business seen.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) came off their lows in late London trade as client business continued to flow despite falls in the local market.
"There has been reasonable two-way business in this market, it is not as black as the screens are showing," said a trader.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed down 0.83 points, 1.19 percent, at 68.52 points, with the premium over the local market at 14.29 percent compared with yesterday's 14.86 percent.
The Indian GDR market had been down 1.50 percent at midday, but recovered to end off just 1.11 percent.

Among gainers, speculative exchange-rate sensitive stocks such as hotels company EIH Ltd added $1.25 to $19.50/$20.50 and Indian Hotels put on $1.00 to $26.00/$27.00, while the big losers were Steel Authority, down 88 cents at $8.25/$9.00 and BSES, off $1.00 at $20.25/$21.25.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index The top 30-share BSE index closed down 33.53 points, or 0.97 percent, at 3,422.35.
"People are nervous about where the local market is going, but there are buyers of GDRs and we have seen some volume, albeit on a day-to-day trading level," said a trader.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended off 0.91 points, 1.30 percent, at 69.14, a premium of 49.02 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index lost 10.68 points to 701.18.

The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended flat at 97.25, a premium of 6.67 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index closed down 33.00 points or 0.46 percent at 7,173.42. -- David Chance London newsroom 44 171 542 5887
